summary: Macro backdrop for ags: mixed (score -1 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates +; dollar −; brl −; mxn −; risk 0; energy +; china 0; breadth 0. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Class III milk +18.4%; weakest: Oats -17.3%. Key releases ahead: US Federal Funds Rate (10-28 2:00 PM ET); US FOMC Statement (10-28 2:00 PM ET); US FOMC Press Conference (10-28 2:30 PM ET); US Advance GDP q/q (10-29 8:30 AM ET); US Core PCE Price Index m/m (10-29 8:30 AM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.99% (-18 bp in a month), 2-year 4.70% (-11 bp); 2s10s curve +29 bp (-7 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 4.02% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 102.33 (+1.1% in a month, +4.1% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.382 (+3.8% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.654 (-0.9%); USD/MXN 18.68 (+5.2%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 +0.6% in a month (+12.9% YTD); VIX 17.2. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 102.64 $/bbl (+15.3% in a month), Brent 111.59, ULSD 4.674 $/gal (+7.0%), natural gas 3.05 (-11.6%). Higher crude lifts biofuel margins (soybean oil, corn for ethanol) and synthetic-fibre costs (supports cotton), but raises diesel, drying and freight costs. Natural gas drives nitrogen fertilizer costs for next year's corn.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper +0.6% in a month, Shanghai Composite -3.7%, Hang Seng -6.3%, yuan +0.9% vs USD. Mixed China signals.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 13 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (39%); S&P GSCI +3.4% in a month; gold -2.7%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
